paras: Turnaround: you get a cream version from a photo or a link, while a filming day waits on a person, a place, and a date.
Cost: a filming day bills the day, the person on camera, and the editing after. A version here draws on the plan you already pay for. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits.

sections.h2: How to Keep a Small Test Fair
paras: Change only one thing between cream versions, so the result points at that one thing.
Worth testing, one at a time: the opening moment, the setting, the shape, the length, and the line you add afterward. Start with the opening. It decides whether anyone sees the rest of the jar.

sections.h2: How the Versions Should Run Together
paras: One campaign gives every cream version the same audience, the same budget, and the same product page.

Many ad accounts let several ads share one group. Some also offer a built-in test that shows each version to part of the audience. The account may spend more on one version early. A version that barely ran has not been tested. Leave the ads as they are while the test is live, so the account keeps counting the same cream test.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold the same plain cream jar in two matched side-by-side positions.

sections.h2: How to Tell Which Version Works
paras: Wait several days, until each cream version has actually played, before you name a winner.

Read three numbers in order. First, how many people stay past the opening. That tells you if the start works. Second, how often people click. That tells you if they wanted to visit. Third, the cost each time someone buys, or adds the jar to the cart. That matters most for the shop. A version can get more views and still lose on sales. If the numbers are close, that change did not matter much. Keep the one you prefer and test a bigger difference next.
sections.alt: Hands rest beside blank color cards and the same plain cream jar.

sections.h2: What the Next Test Should Change
paras: You keep the cream version that brings sales at a cost you can accept, turn off the clear losers, and change one new thing.

Write down the date, what changed, and the result. After a few rounds you will see what your buyers respond to. When a winner starts costing more per sale, make fresh versions of the jar. Work through the opening, the setting, the shape, the length, then the offer. Each round starts from what already worked.

faq.q: What is a video ad you can test?
faq.a: A short paid-ad file of a product you already sell. For the cream, you bring the jar photo, and you name the first second. The crew stays off the calendar for that test.

faq.q: What should I look for when I pick a tool for ad tests?
faq.a: Pick a tool that can make a second opening of the same cream from the photo you already have, with no new shoot.

faq.q: Do I pay to make each version?
faq.a: Yes. A clip is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark. It can run as a paid placement and sit on the product page. You can run it without a separate permission form.

faq.q: Which frames can I download, and where can they run?
faq.a: Use 9:16 when the test runs on a phone screen, 1:1 when it sits in a feed, and 16:9 when the screen is wide. 4:3 and 3:4 are only for a placement that lists them. A second shape is a different test.

faq.q: Can I test ads for multiple products at once?
faq.a: Yes, if each cream jar has its own photo. Reuse one opening as the note, and let an API start a file when a new jar arrives. Many jars still means one file each.

faq.q: Should I stop filming with people I hire?
faq.a: No. Keep a filmed spot when you want a person you hired on camera. Use a generated file when you are still choosing the first second. They answer different questions.

faq.q: Can a generated ad be turned down by the ad account?
faq.a: It can, for the same reasons any ad can. If the line sounds like a customer wrote a review, say so the way that app currently asks you to. Rules change, so read them before you raise the budget.

faq.q: How many versions should a small shop run?
faq.a: Start with a few, often three. More than that splits a small budget so far that no version gets a fair chance to play. Every extra version is another file.
The opening. It decides whether anyone watches the rest. Keep the jar, the length, and the shape the same until that result is clear.

faq.q: Can I change the price on only one version?
faq.a: No. While you are testing the video or the photo, put the same words, the same price, and the same music on every file. Test the offer in a later round, on its own.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: From the ad account, after each version has played. The test does not invent a winner. You read who stayed, who clicked, and what a sale cost.

faq.q: What if the ad account barely shows one version?
faq.a: That version was not tested. Wait until each file has had a real chance to play, or the comparison is noise.

faq.q: Do I have to say the presenter is generated?
faq.a: Yes, when the ad could be read as a real customer's review. Follow that platform's disclosure rule. Give the AI actor a name you chose for the shop.
